 Rain and possible thunderstorms are expected in Magnolia on Halloween, followed by warmer, generally drier weather Sunday and Monday. Daylight saving time ends early Sunday, bringing an earlier sunset.
 CLICK HERE to see our weather page . 
 THREE-DAY FORECAST 
 Saturday, October 31: Periods of rain, with thunderstorms possible during the evening. The high will be near 67 degrees and the low around 60. Rain chances are high, and outdoor Halloween activities could be affected.
 Sunday, November 1: Lingering overnight thunderstorms should give way to intervals of clouds and sunshine. The high will reach approximately 75 degrees, with a low near 60. Daytime rain chances diminish considerably.
 Monday, November 2: Mostly cloudy, humid conditions are forecast, with a high near 77 degrees and a low around 65. Rain chances remain relatively low during daylight hours, although showers become more possible later.
 SUNRISE AND SUNSET 
 Day                     Sunrise               Sunset 
 Saturday             7:30 a.m.             6:21 p.m.
 Sunday                6:31 a.m.            5:21 p.m.
 Monday                6:32 a.m.            5:20 p.m.
 Clocks move backward one hour at 2 a.m. Sunday. Saturday times are Central Daylight Time; Sunday and Monday times are Central Standard Time.
 MOONRISE AND MOONSET 
 Day                      Moonrise            Moonset 
 Saturday              11:40 p.m.           1:26 p.m.
 Sunday                11:50 p.m.           1:08 p.m.
 Monday                No moonrise         1:43 p.m.
 The moonrise occurs late in the evening Saturday and Sunday. Monday has no moonrise within the calendar day; the next rise occurs after midnight. Times reflect the daylight-saving transition.
 TROPICAL WEATHER 
 The National Hurricane Center reported no active tropical cyclones or disturbances in the Atlantic Ocean, Caribbean Sea or Gulf of Mexico. Its 7 a.m. CDT Saturday outlook indicated that tropical cyclone formation was not expected during the next seven days.
 SPACE WEATHER 
 NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center forecasts possible G1, or minor, geomagnetic storm conditions during the October 31–November 2 period, with a maximum predicted Kp index of 4.67. Such activity can affect some radio communications and satellite operations.
 The preceding 24-hour observed maximum was Kp 4, below storm levels.
 MAGNOLIA OBSERVATORY 
 The Moon reaches its last-quarter phase Sunday, November 1, at approximately 2:28 p.m. Its illuminated portion decreases from about 66 percent Saturday to 43 percent Monday.
 The waning Moon will be prominent during the late-night and morning hours. Cloud cover, particularly Saturday, could limit viewing.
 EARTHQUAKES 
 The USGS magnitude 2.5-plus earthquake feed reports no earthquakes in Arkansas, Louisiana, Texas, Oklahoma, Missouri, Tennessee and Mississippi during the past 24 hours.
 FIREBALLS 
 The American Meteor Society fireball database reports no fireball sightings within 500 miles of Magnolia in the past 24 hours.
 INTERNATIONAL SPACE STATION 
 There will be no bright pass of the International Space Station over Magnolia in the next three days.
 U.S. SPACECRAFT LAUNCHES 
 SpaceX's Starlink Group 15-18 Falcon 9 mission was scheduled from Vandenberg Space Force Base, California, at approximately 11:02 p.m. Friday, October 30. A subsequent Space Force mission, USSF-432, is scheduled for 7:42 p.m. Monday, November 2.
